definitions.gloss: dark ink; thick, deep-black sumi ink
definitions.explanation: Sumi ink ground to a deep, dark black, as opposed to {薄墨|うすずみ} (pale, watered-down ink). Used in calligraphy and traditional writing, and standard for congratulatory or formal correspondence.

examples.japanese: {濃墨|こずみ}で{名前|なまえ}を{書|か}く。
examples.english: I write the name in dark ink.

examples.japanese: お{祝|いわ}いの{手紙|てがみ}は{濃墨|こずみ}で{書|か}くのが{礼儀|れいぎ}だ。
examples.english: It is proper etiquette to write congratulatory letters in dark ink.

examples.japanese: {書道|しょどう}の{先生|せんせい}は、{力強|ちからづよ}い{線|せん}には{濃墨|こずみ}が{欠|か}かせないと{言|い}った。
examples.english: The calligraphy teacher said that dark ink is essential for powerful strokes.

notes:
The counterpart of {薄墨|うすずみ} (pale ink). In traditional correspondence the depth of the ink carries meaning: deep black ink is used for happy or formal occasions, while pale ink signals mourning.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {濃墨|こずみ}で{書|か}く: to write in dark ink
- {濃墨|こずみ}を{磨|す}る: to grind (make) dark ink

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {薄墨|うすずみ}: pale ink — watered-down gray ink, used for condolence letters.
- {墨汁|ぼくじゅう}: liquid sumi ink — ready-made bottled ink, as opposed to ink ground from an inkstick.
